content.text:
I identified **mp-1271345 (Cr2NiO4)** as the only phase present.

1. **Single-phase fits:** I fitted each of the nine candidates on its own. Cr2NiO4 gave an R-factor of 0.44 at 0 % strain. Every other candidate gave an R-factor between 0.98 and 1.01, so none of them describes the pattern.
2. **Residual after Cr2NiO4:** After the fit, nothing left over is bigger than 19 % of the strongest observed peak. It shows up as paired positive and negative wiggles around the main peaks (near 33°, 41–43° and 59–64°). That pattern looks like a peak-shape or position mismatch, not new peaks from another phase.
3. **Two-phase fits:** Adding the Li–Mn–Ni oxide (mp-762624) or TmNiO3 (mp-1106304) to Cr2NiO4 gave each one only 2–4 % of the weight. The R-factor barely moved, from 0.444 to 0.443 and 0.442. I only tried those two partners, but every other candidate fitted so poorly alone that a meaningful second phase is unlikely.

{"present": ["mp-1271345"], "confidence": 0.85, "note": "Cr2NiO4 alone fits with R=0.44 versus at least 0.98 for every other candidate, and adding a second phase does not improve the fit or leave structured leftover peaks."}
